amendments.rule: Where one Hebrew substantive is rendered by a multi-word English phrase, head it on the word carrying the lexeme rather than on the word the ASV supplies to complete the phrase. Decide which is which by dropping each word in turn: the head is the one whose loss loses the lexeme. `יַבָּשָׁה` → *dry land* heads on *dry*, because *land* alone is any land; `בָּמָה` → *high place*, *high places* heads on *high*, because *place* alone is any place; so too `קֹדֶשׁ` → *holy place*, `מִסְתָּר` → *secret places*, `תִּמֹרָה` → *palm trees*, `עֹלָה` → *burnt offerings*. **Neither part of speech nor position decides this.** The supplied word is usually the English phrase's head noun and the lexeme-bearing word usually an attributive adjective standing first, but do not move a head onto a generic noun merely because it is the noun — that reasoning would head *dry land* on *land* — and do not reach for the first word as a rule. Where the ASV supplies the modifier instead, the same test moves the head the other way: `תַּנִּין` → *sea monsters* heads on *monsters*, because *sea* is a specifier added to a word that already names the creature. **Where the subtraction test ties, read the ASV's own use of the English noun.** A class noun the ASV writes alone for a Hebrew word of that same class — in the verse, in the passage, or as its ordinary rendering of the word before you — is not a supplied generic but the word that realizes the lexeme, and a modifier standing beside it is the ASV's specifier distinguishing one class word from another, so the head stays on the class noun: JOB.4.10-11 writes a bare *lion* for `אַרְיֵה` and *the fierce lion*, *the young lions* and *The old lion* for `שַׁחַל`, `כְּפִיר` and `לַיִשׁ`, and all four head on *lion*; JOB.4.17 writes *a man* for `גֶּבֶר` and *mortal man* for `אֱנוֹשׁ`, and both head on *man*; `יֶתֶר` → *tent cord* heads on *cord*. Where the ASV never writes that noun alone for the word — *place* for `בָּמָה`, *sleep* for `תַּרְדֵּמָה` → *deep sleep* — the noun is the supplied generic and the head is the modifier, as above. Ask which of the two the English noun is before choosing, and say in the note that the other reading was available. Where the phrase also carries an article, *of*, or *a*, rules 19 and 29 place those; they are never the head. **But read whether a second source nominal stands in the phrase before sending that *of* to rule 19.** What that rule places is the relation between two nominals the Hebrew writes, and an *of* the ASV writes inside a phrase it has supplied for a single substantive is not that. Where the ASV completes the substantive with a generic head noun and writes an *of* between that noun and the word carrying the lexeme — `זָהָב` → ***things of*** *gold*, `עֵץ` → ***things of*** *wood* — the supplied noun and its *of* both join that substantive's unit, neither is `added`, and the head stays on the word carrying the lexeme, so those two head on *gold* and *wood*. This is what rule 46 already gives a bare participle or adjective in giving its supplied noun phrase *whatever article, relative or* of *the phrase needs*, holding for a substantive of any kind. Decide it by the subtraction test above: drop the English *of* and ask whether a relation between two source nouns has gone unstated, or whether only a phrase the ASV supplied for one noun has been broken in two. Where a second source nominal does stand, rule 19 governs as before and the *of* is the rectum's, whatever generic the ASV supplied to expand the first noun — `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any kind* ***of*** *tree* gives *of tree* to the rectum while `כֹּל` keeps *any kind* — and an ASV italic on the supplied words corroborates the supply and decides nothing, by rule 7. Two riders. An article morpheme standing before such a phrase takes the written *the* under rules 29 and 47, a present morpheme taking its English before a supplied reading does, so `לָעֵצִים` → *for* ***the*** *things of wood* gives the *the* to the article and *things of wood* to the noun. And a preposition the ASV writes before the whole phrase to state what it contributes to its clause is its own morpheme's, or rule 33's where no preposition morpheme stands, and is no part of the supplied expression. **A substantival numeral is such a substantive.** Where the ASV completes a numeral standing for what it counts with a generic noun the Hebrew does not write, that noun joins the numeral's unit and the head stays on the numeral, which carries the lexeme: `אֶחָד` → *one* ***portion*** in a list of tribal allotments, `אֶחָד` → *the* ***first day***. Rule 33's `added` case is the other one, and what the supplied noun does tells them apart: there the numeral is a quantity whose English is already complete and the noun names the unit it is counted in — the italic ***reeds*** after *five and twenty thousand* — so the numeral's own rendering loses nothing when it is dropped.
amendments.why: Rule 31 sends an *of* standing in the supplied phrase to rule 19, but rule 19 places only the relation between two nominals the Hebrew writes. Where the ASV supplies both a generic head noun and an *of* before a single source noun, that cross-reference has nothing to act on, and a reader following it literally must either invent a construct relation or mark the *of* `added` while the noun it belongs to stands beside it. 1CH.29.2 and 29.5 write that shape seven times over the metal list (*the gold for the things of gold*, and so for silver, brass, iron and wood), and the chapter had to settle it without a rule. The amendment states the answer rule 46 already gives for a bare participle or adjective — the supplied noun phrase joins the substantive's unit with whatever article, relative or *of* it needs — and extends it to a substantive of any kind, while leaving rule 19 untouched wherever a second source nominal stands: `כֹּל אֶבֶן יְקָרָה` → *all manner of precious stones* at 29.2 still gives its *of* to the rectum, as rule 19's own `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any kind of tree* directs. Nothing in the corpus tables contradicts it; the `כֹּל` → *all manner of* units there are the two-nominal case rule 19 governs, and the amendment does not reach them. The two riders record the chapter's other two decisions in the same phrase: the written article takes the *the* (29.2, 29.5), and the preposition heading the phrase keeps its own word.

conventions: A possessive לְ with a pronominal suffix that the ASV renders by a single English possessive pronoun is rule 49's fused genitive and not a split pair: לְךָ → *Thine* (29.11, twice) and *thine own* (29.16) put the preposition and the suffix in one unit, headed on the suffix and on the English pronoun, since no English word is spent on either morpheme alone. The clause's construction-supplied copula joins that fused unit, exactly as it joins לַיהוָה → *is Jehovah's*, and an intensifying *own* belongs to it under rule 18. The vocative and the predicate nominal standing beside it keep only their own English.

report: Checked all 61 candidate lemma groups and read the 30-verse dump end to end for the split the table cannot see - a supplied English word marked `added` in one verse and folded into a licensing morpheme in another. No genuine split found, so patches is empty.

Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by what the ASV wrote. לְעֵינֵי fuses to *before* at 29.10 and splits at 29.25, where *in the sight of* spends a word on each morpheme - rule 30's one-rendering condition read in both directions. מִיָּדְךָ fuses to *of* at 29.14 and splits at 29.16 where *hand* is written. לְ before an infinitive construct takes the written *to* at 29.4, 29.5, 29.14, 29.16 and 29.19 and is `unrepresented` at 29.17, where the ASV writes a bare complement (*seen ... offer willingly*).

Construct-chain determiners are consistent across all three of rule 29's cases: fronting where the rectum is anarthrous (29.6 *the captains of thousands*, 29.24 *the sons ... of king David*), nothing fronted where it is arthrous (29.4, 29.6 *the princes of the fathers houses*, 29.30), and the possessive count at 29.6 *the king's work*. The multi-level chain עֲבוֹדַת בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִים at 29.7 divides exactly as rule 29's אֹצְרוֹת בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִים does: the article's *the* before *house*, a supplied *the* on the outer construct.

The 17 `added` units hold together as a class - a supplied word is `added` only where no morpheme licenses it, and goes to the licensing morpheme wherever one stands. Supplied *that* at 29.3 and 29.11 against the written אֲשֶׁר at 29.16, 29.25, 29.27 and 29.30; appositional *even* at 29.4 and 29.21, in verses where no object marker stands; supplied object pronouns at 29.3, 29.8 and 29.22 where no object morpheme is written; *As for* at 29.17 under rule 16's own limit.

Three groups look like splits and are not. שַׂר at 29.6 is *the princes* once and bare *captains* once because one phrase writes two English *the*s and the other writes one. הוּא is *that* at 29.21 and 29.22 (demonstrative taking the phrase's determiner) and `unrepresented` at 29.16 (resumptive pronoun of a tripartite clause, rule 20). דָּבָר is *the acts* once and *the history* three times inside one verse, 29.29, because the ASV wrote different English for one lemma.

Waw connectives: 101 occurrences, all read off the ASV as rule 14 directs. The count against the ASV's connectives is run in both directions - the surplus waw of the numeral phrase at 29.7 is `unrepresented` and the surplus *and* between two juxtaposed numeral phrases at 29.21 is `added`, both under rule 42. The correlative *Both ... and* at 29.12 is not one pair on one morpheme: two waws stand in the phrase and each takes the word standing where it stands.

BSB: 31 disagreements, none a genuine error. The two recurring classes are the documented convention differences - 13 R tokens the ASV's recasting leaves nothing for (rule 40) and 13 Td tokens for which the ASV writes no *the* (rule 29). Of the six singletons, the cohortative he at 29.18 is rule 32's own named case, the resumptive הוּא at 29.16 is rule 20's tripartite clause, the waw at 29.7 is rule 42's surplus, the לַ at 29.20 is a bare English object, and the וְ + כִּי pair at 29.14 is two morphemes with one written connective, the waw taking the *But* that stands where it stands.

The report's 28 repeated notes were reviewed for the convention log; all but one restate a contract rule the verse pass had already cited, so recording them would bury the one that matters. The single chapter-wide judgment recorded is the fused possessive לְ + suffix at 29.11 (twice) and 29.16.
